title: Mornings with Graham & Emmy
teaser: Nessel fights secret DTE contracts for OpenAI/Oracle project; what it means for your bills.

lines.text: Good morning and welcome to Mornings with Graham & Emmy — the Michigan Data Wire, your podcast on Michigan's data center buildout. I'm Graham.
And I'm Emmy.

Today we're talking about Attorney General Dana Nessel taking the fight for transparency straight to the Court of Appeals over those secret DTE contracts tied to the big OpenAI and Oracle hyperscale project in Saline.
This feels like it could set a precedent for the whole state, Graham. Why is she pushing so hard right now?

She's arguing that ratepayers deserve to know the terms and costs before anything gets locked in. The contracts are hidden, and if the details stay secret, folks could end up with higher electric bills and lost tax revenue.
How does this connect to everything else happening around Michigan lately?

It's part of a bigger wave. Just yesterday Pere Marquette Township enacted a one-year moratorium on new data centers over energy and water concerns. Manistee Township joined a pause on Friday. Cass County residents packed a hall yesterday worried about noise, water use, and rising bills.
And now new state rules on Great Lakes water pulls that these facilities need millions of gallons for daily cooling. It all seems to be coming to a head.
Exactly. Nessel's move today could force more openness on how these projects get approved, which might slow things down or change the economics for developers.
Who are the main players here besides Nessel and DTE?

OpenAI and Oracle are behind the hyperscale project in Washtenaw County. Local residents and townships are pushing back hard on the impacts to farmland, water supplies, and utility rates that could ripple out thirty miles or more.
What kind of history is behind these fights? Have we seen similar battles before?

Data centers have been landing in Michigan for a while now, often with big power demands that strain the grid. Townships are responding with pauses and zoning changes because once land is optioned, it's hard to walk back.
And the water angle — how much is really at stake with the new tracking rules?

The state just posted updated diversion tracking that directly limits how much large cooling operations can take from the Great Lakes basin. Projects in several counties would need millions of gallons daily, so this becomes a real choke point.
If the court reopens the hearing, what happens next for ratepayers?

More transparency could mean better scrutiny of who pays for infrastructure upgrades and whether hidden deals shift costs onto regular customers. It might also set rules that apply statewide for future approvals.
Sounds like this could influence those upcoming meetings in Coldwater and Kalamazoo tomorrow.

Absolutely. Let's move to quick hits. Saline Township just hired a retired sergeant to manage zoning applications for big industrial projects, including potential data centers. Residents near Ann Arbor now have a direct contact point.

That signals they're expecting more complex cases ahead. Meanwhile in Dowagiac, neighbors are suing a former crypto site now run by Alliance Cloud Services over nonstop high-pitched noise that violates new city limits.

And Cass County residents packed a town hall yesterday pushing officials to reject or restrict projects before more land gets optioned. Indirect rate hikes could hit people thirty miles away on the same grid.
Coldwater area townships are hosting their first public briefing tomorrow on proposed data centers, covering power, water, and tax impacts. Nearby communities are already weighing similar projects.
Coldwater is also readying permanent zoning rules to shield neighborhoods from noise and utility strain, with no projects proposed yet.

On deck for tomorrow, August 17: Coldwater City Council, Planning Commission, and Board of Public Utilities are holding a joint informational meeting on data center impacts, zoning, and potential ordinances.
The City of Coldwater Planning Commission and CBPU Board will discuss zoning and regulation of high-utility data centers at the same time.
Caledonia Township Planning Commission has a data center ordinance discussion and potential zoning amendments on the agenda.
And Kalamazoo City Commission will vote on a resolution for a temporary moratorium on data center development.
Plenty for folks to weigh in on if they're in driving distance.
Full sources and the live map at the Michigan Data Center Tracker. We're back tomorrow.

episode_title: AG Nessel Pushes Transparency on Saline Data Center Deals Amid Statewide Pushback
